registered_at: 2026-10-23, before any script, feature or outcome
batch: untested-categories 2026-10-23 (operator: 'I want to test all of these')
study: Analyst upgrades during regular hours: buy one minute after the headline, hold 20 minutes (Bradley, Clarke, Lee & Ornthanalai 2014, J. Finance: +1.83% over 30 minutes with newswire timestamps; Chen 2009: drift lasts ~20 minutes).
source: Bradley et al. 2014; the move is fast and timestamp-sensitive. Our news study (10/15) pooled all headlines and found the reaction in the headline minute; upgrades alone were not scored.
prior: LOW (~10%): the free feed's speed was the problem in the news study.
data: Alpaca news (Benzinga) 2025-10-01 .. 2026-10-15, headlines matching (case-insensitive) 'upgrade' AND NOT 'downgrade', with exactly one symbol, created_at within 09:45..15:30 ET; SIP 1-minute bars for that name-day (data-only account).
trade: Buy at the open of the first 1-minute bar starting >= T + 60 s; sell at the close of the bar 20 minutes later. Price >= $10.
control: Same name, a seeded random minute in the same clock hour on the 5 previous sessions where it traded (mean of available), same 20-minute hold (seed 'upg-ctrl').
primary: LIFT = event return - control; event-equal within day, day-equal across days; day-clustered t. Halves: A = 2025-10-01 .. 2026-04-15, B = 2026-04-16 .. 2026-10-15.
pass: In BOTH halves: LIFT >= +5 bp with t >= 2.0 AND event mean net (after 5 bp) > 0. Floors: >= 150 events and >= 30 days per half (smaller than other studies: events are rare; declared).
information_only: entry at T + 1 s (the reaction itself)
the T -> T+60 s move (what the feed delay costs)
no_retuning: Keyword rule, 60 s delay, 20-minute hold, cost fixed.

common.halves: Warehouse studies: A = 2026-05-11 .. 2026-07-29, B = 2026-07-30 .. 2026-10-15 (110 sessions; 2026-04-27 .. 05-08 are warm-up for look-backs only).
common.statistic_default: Per half: per day, the mean over that day's trades of the measured quantity; day-equal mean; day-clustered t (df = days - 1).
common.cost: 5 bp round trip binding (the desk's current RT cost on $20+ names is ~3 bp); net also printed at 3, 10, 20 bp.
common.price_floor: entry price >= $10 primary; >= $20 (the desk's live floor) as information.
common.confirmation: A PASS is re-run unchanged on warehouse_confirm (2026-01-14 .. 04-24, held out, never read) before anything else; then a forward paper prereg. Never a desk change by itself; the desk stays frozen for the floor20 window.
common.power: Outcome-blind count step first: trades and days per half, and a projected MDE from the dispersion of the CONTROL leg only; floors per half >= 300 trades and >= 20 days, MDE <= the lift bar, else UNDERPOWERED with no outcome read.
common.fail_rule: FAIL: t <= -2 in a half, or the 97.5% upper bound of the lift below the bar in both halves. Otherwise not passed = UNDERPOWERED.
common.data_account: All fetches on the data-only Alpaca account (secrets_data.json), never the desk key; paced; no paid data.
common.multiplicity: Eight studies registered together on 2026-10-23 (the 'untested categories' batch). Each has ONE primary; a family-wise reading is printed: a primary counts as a batch PASS only with t >= 2.73 (Bonferroni 0.05/8, two-sided, normal approx) in both halves; t >= 2 in both halves without that is reported as 'PASS (single-test), not batch-robust'.
amended: (C1) Cross-sectional studies (no control leg): the power MDE comes from a PLACEBO - a seeded random set of the same size as the long set each day (seed '<study>-placebo') minus the all-eligible mean; MDE = (t 2.0 + 0.84) x SD(day placebo LIFT) / sqrt(days). The placebo is outcome-free with respect to the signal.

(C2) No eligibility test may use a bar after entry. Exit price = the close of the last bar at or before the exit minute; a name lacking the exit-minute bar is NOT skipped. A name lacking its entry bar is skipped (counted) - the entry bar is known at entry.
(C3) Confirmation window for fresh-fetch studies: 2026-01-14 .. 2026-04-24 (the warehouse_confirm dates), fetched ONLY after a PASS, never before; no study's scored halves may include it.
(C4) Every fetch logs symbols dropped by rate-limit errors (429) after retries; a half with any unrecovered drop is refused (rerun the fetch).

Universe fact (declared): the warehouse is NOT book-like - it is every liquid name (prior-day raw close >= $10, 20-day mean dollar volume >= $20M, active and inactive, ~1,840-1,950 per day); bars end at 15:59 (no closing auction).

amended.when: 2026-10-23, after result-skeptic round 1 FIX FIRST, before any script or data read.
changes: (1) First matching headline per name-day only.
(2) Before any outcome: hand-check 30 seeded matches (seed 'upg-hand'); if > 10% are not stock-rating upgrades, the keyword rule is tightened ONCE (written down) and re-checked on 30 fresh seeds.
(3) Liquidity: 20-day mean dollar volume >= $20M and prior close >= $10 (the warehouse rule).
(4) Exit = close of bar e+19 (e = entry bar), last bar at or before per C2; the price floor is the entry bar open.
(5) Event and control returns are each SPY-adjusted (minus SPY's return over the same minutes).
(7) Declared: the 10/15 news study (NEWS_UP, all headlines) already failed; upgrades alone were never scored.

amended_2.when: 2026-10-23, after result-skeptic round 2 (final), before any script or data read. Each choice is the strict option: no look-back, warm-up or control touches the held-out window 2026-01-14 .. 04-24.
changes: (3) Control sessions must lie inside the same half's window (and for the confirmation run, inside 01-14 .. 04-24); use the mean of up to 5 previous in-window sessions, minimum 3, else the event is skipped and counted.

amended_3.when: 2026-10-23, after result-skeptic CODE review round 1, before any bars are fetched and before any outcome (the partial 09:30-start news cache was deleted).
changes: (1) News is fetched from 00:00 ET; the FIRST matching single-symbol headline of the whole day defines the name-day; it is an event only if created in [09:45:00, 15:30:00) (an earlier first upgrade means no event).
(2) Control minutes start at 09:46 (no pre-market), same clock hour, ending by 15:59; control days exclude the name's own upgrade days and stay inside the half.
(3) POWER: MDE = (2.0 + 0.84) x SD(day mean of (one seeded control draw - the ctrl2 mean)) / sqrt(days).
(4) Prices are RAW (unadjusted) for the $10 floor and the returns.
(5) Liquidity look-back stays inside the half: an event needs 20 in-half daily bars before its day (B events start ~2026-05-26); no held-out data is fetched.
(6) C4: a missing news day, a 400-page cap hit, a missing bars file or a partial SPY file stops the run.

(7) HANDCHECK: --handcheck writes handcheck.json (30 seeded ids, the reviewer's count of non stock-rating upgrades, the matching-rule hash); the count step and --score refuse without it or if more than 3 of 30 are not stock upgrades.
(8) FAIL is on the lift only (t <= -2, or both upper bounds < 5 bp); batch-robust bar t >= 2.84 (11 studies); net is SPY-adjusted, and the unhedged net is printed as information.
(9) Entry bar must start by 15:40; microsecond-safe rounding; created strictly before 15:30:00.

amended_4.when: 2026-10-24 ~03:55 ET, during the bar fetch, before any outcome; data handling only.
changes: Events need a US-listed ticker symbol (1-5 capitals, optional .X class suffix); foreign listings such as 'TSX:ENB' are dropped (the US SIP feed cannot trade them).
An event on its half's first trading day has no in-half daily look-back; no daily request is made (it fails the 20-bar liquidity rule, as amended_3 (5) already implies).
